Studies of HF regeneration are increasingly significant due to the prevalence of alopecia and the recognized contribution of HFs to wound healing [1]. Understanding the mechanism that governs HF morphogenesis is essential for the reconstruction of functional HFs. The development of HF during embryogenesis shares the same driving force with the kidney, lung and tooth, known as epithelial-mesenchymal interactions (EMIs) [2, 3]. Owing to ethical constraints in human studies, knowledge of HF organogenesis is based mainly on mice.
